All other character positions are filled with space characters." / "The common part of the variable-length groups is now moved according to the rules for variable-length groups of equal length, as defined in General rule 9a above." / "NOTE 4  If the receiving table is an occurs-depending table, ..." — then, back at the outer level, "10) Additional rules and explanations relative to this statement are given in 14.6.10, Overlapping operands."
findings.markdown_says: Every one of those blocks is written flush left with no indentation (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 28695-28707): "If the sending group is longer than the receiving group, ...", "1. If the data item to be space-filled is a dynamic-length elementary item, ...", "2. ...", "3. All other character positions are filled with space characters.", "The common part of the variable-length groups is now moved ...", "NOTE 4 ...", immediately followed by the flush-left "10) Additional rules and explanations ...". The same transcription indents correctly on the facing page (page 701 uses "   a) If the groups are of equal length:" and "      The content of each character position ...").
findings.why_it_matters: The recursive space-filling procedure (items 1-3), the 'common part' paragraph and NOTE 4 are sub-items of General rule 9)b); the page break detaches them from their parent. Flush left they read as peers of the outer general rules 1)-10), so the 1./2./3. procedure appears to be a free-standing rule that always applies rather than one that applies only to unequal-length variable-length group moves, and 'as defined in General rule 9a above' loses its anchor. Rule 9 is the variable-length group MOVE rule the compiler implements, so mis-scoping it changes which moves space-fill.
findings.suggested_repair: Indent the seven blocks between 'If the sending group is longer...' and 'NOTE 4 ...' to the 9)b) sub-level (matching the 3-space / 6-space convention used on page 701), leaving '10) Additional rules and explanations...' flush left.
